Breast Implant Illness [5855]

By: Carol Albertyn Christie | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

Summary:
Breast implant illness (BII) is a term that some women and doctors use to refer to a wide range of symptoms that can develop after undergoing reconstruction or cosmetic augmentation with breast implants. It is also sometimes referred to as autoimmune/inflammatory syndrome induced by adjuvants (ASIA). BII can occur with any type of breast implant, including silicone gel-filled, saline-filled, smooth surface, textured surface, round, or teardrop-shaped.Two possible problems with breast implants:
One is the condition Towt developed — breast implant illness (BII) — a cluster of symptoms such as fatigue, memory loss, and joint pain that can occur after getting breast implants and that frequently improve after the removal of the implants (explantation). Many of the symptoms of BII are the same as those of autoimmune and connective tissue disorders, such as lupus and rheumatoid arthritis. However, only some people who have BII get diagnosed with a specific autoimmune or connective tissue disorder. BII isn’t well understood and isn’t officially recognized as a medical condition, but some experts say it’s likely to be related to an autoimmune reaction to the implants.
The other serious risk is a rare form of T-cell lymphoma (cancer of the immune system) called breast implant-associated anaplastic large cell lymphoma (BIA-ALCL) that develops in the scar tissue and fluid surrounding an implant. So far, all the confirmed cases of BIA-ALCL have been in women who had breast implants with a textured surface or whose implant surface type was not known. BIA-ALCL is curable in most patients if it’s diagnosed early and treated appropriately, but at least 33 women have died from the illness as of July 2019.2 Some patient activists call BIA-ALCL a “man-made cancer” because it’s linked to a specific medical device and was identified for the first time in 1997.



Further information:
Debbie Frost’s Story – 58 Cape Town completely flat chested and in 1997 at the age of 35 she decided she wanted breast implants. She was initially very happy with the results but says that not long after she started with head aches.Never once thought of the connection between implants and major changes.A sense of frustration and desperation over the years as literally every single doctor, medical or otherwise gave me the diagnosis of Chronic Fatigue, stress or depression, and in later years menopause, fibromyalgia. I absolutely refused to accept these explanations and always felt defeated after an appointment that I had been hopeful about. The prescriptions would be handed to me, cortisone, anti-depressants, pain medication etc, but not once did I fill them – the prescriptions would be torn up before I even got home. A lot of energy went on hiding the fact that I felt so awful as I just didn’t want to be that mother/wife that always had headaches or was always sick. I was always anxious about being labeled a hypochondriac. I was also anxious about not being able to live in the moment or do things spontaneously. I didn’t want to say yes to something only to wake up and find I was too sick that day and have to cancel, so I just started to withdraw altogether.There are many occasions that I just had to get through but it always felt like I was in a bubble – just holding it together to get through it. In the later years I would take anti inflammatories before an occasion, just to get rid of some of the swelling in my face. I became completely intolerant to any form of vitamin or supplement and to any form of alcohol or preservative. I do feel disappointed by some of the people that treated me. After my first surgery in Oct 2018 my GP was incredibly supportive when I found out about BII and was really interested to talk about it and for both of us to find out more. When I started to get flu like symptoms again and expressed my concern that I knew some capsule had been left behind as it was difficult to reach, and that I thought that was what was wrong, he actually lost interest in me and basically told me that I needed to ‘move on’ and get on with my life. I was pretty much on my own again! Googling my symptoms (again) one evening I came across BII and found the site Healing Breast Implant Illness – it literally saved my life.I had my implants removed on 8 October 2018. Both implants were ruptured. I made a fairly quick recovery and felt positive and soooo happy to be free of the implants. After a few weeks I felt a lot better – far less dizziness and brain fog and less neck pain and nausea. After a couple of months I started to feel the awful flu like symptoms, the dizziness etc. I was put on antibiotics twice for a suspected bladder infection (I don’t think I ever had one) and did actually feel better for a short time after each course. By April 2019 I was convinced that I didn’t have long to live and that a diagnosis would soon be given. I almost felt that it would be a welcome relief to be told I only had a few months to live as I was just exhausted and I just couldn’t carry on.The surgeon who did my explants couldn’t see me until late August and assured me that the capsule was not the source of my problems. I had done a lot more research by then and I knew that the capsule was DEFINITELY the source of my problems. By now I had also found the South African sister site of Healing Breast Implant Illness and had a lot of help from the ladies on this site.I saw a string of top CT Plastic Surgeons who advised me to return to my original surgeon and they all confirmed that the capsule was not a problem and sometimes actually dangerous to remove.
I finally found a PS that actually listened to my story and was prepared to re-operate. He also stated that the capsule can ALWAYS be found and removed, no matter how difficult. The care that I received at this practice was second to none and I will always be extremely grateful to this surgeon and his whole team.The operation was really very painful and it took at least a month before I started to feel strong enough to do anything. The improvements were slow but noticeable. As the nausea abated my appetite returned which was such a fantastic feeling.
Kalina Chiminello’s Story – Johannesburg
Kalina was also flat chested and had her implants at 19.BREAST IMPLANTS ARE NOT SAFE!Those of you who have breast implants, are thinking about getting them or know someone who has them, this post is for you.23 September is a date I will celebrate every year going forward as the date of my re-birth. The day of my breast explant surgery. The day I was given a second chance at life!If you had told me a few years ago that my breast implants were slowly killing me I would have thought you were crazy and completely brushed you off. I would have told you these were one of the best purchases I had ever made. They had given me boost of self confidence which was priceless to me.I had my first breast augmentation surgery in 2005 when I was 19 years old. Looking back, my health started to decline within the first year. It began with random symptoms which I would NEVER have linked to the my breast implants. Unexplained rashes on my face and body, hives, hyperpigmentation, sudden intolerance to the sun, intolerance to extreme temperatures, ovrian cysts, blurred vision and the list goes on... As the years went by the symptoms intensified and new ones kept popping up. Brain fog (which was at times so bad I could hardly string a sentence together), extreme fatigue, heart palpitations, food intolerances, joint pain, muscle spasms, rapid aging of the skin, hair loss, vision problems, swollen lymph nodes, discoloured and freezing hands and feet, abdomial pain and neuropathy just to name a few. As my health declined I saw tons of specialists. Most tests came back normal. The only things found were that I tested positive for anti nuclear antibodies, a sign my body was attacking itself. My thyroid was affected too, T3 and T4 levels were way off. The doctors had no idea why I was falling apart. They said it looked like I was developing an autoimmune disease. I was tested for MS, Lupus, connective tissue diseases, Sjorgens etc... whatever I had was mimicking all of these but was none of them... After years of tests and hundreds of thousands spent I finally gave up on finding answers and just learned to live with it.
Not one of my doctors had ever mentioned that this could me my problem. WHY???? The answer is quite simple actually - because it's in none of their textbooks...As I began to seach for more answers I found a Facebook group called BREAST IMPLANT ILLNESS AND HEALING BY NICOLE. This group has over 126000 members and is growing with thousands each month. I literally dropped to my knees and sobbed uncontrollably. As I read every story I felt I was reading my own. I was no longer alone. There was an answer. I HAD BREAST IMPLANT ILLNESS! These women were getting their implants removed (via a PROPER EXPLANT) and their symptoms were reversing. These incredible souls were my lifeline - the knowledge they shared, the support, the love, the compassion were the most priceless gifts I have received on this journey. The explanation was quite simple really. My body was being attacked on two fronts. Firstly, two massive foreign objects filled with absolute garbage had been placed in my chest which don't belong there... so every minute, of every hour, of every day my body was fighting to get them out. My immune system started getting tired and confused after a while and my body started attacking itself. Secondly, implants are made up of over 40 different chemicals and heavy metals which had started leeching into my bloodstream and affecting and disrupting literally every single system in my body. These chemicals are carcinogens, neurotoxins and endocrine disruptors and they had been placed on top of my vital organs! It made perfect sense.
I am a numbers person and I decided to do a heavy metals analysis to check if I had any issues there. I HAVE 99% VANADIUM AND 96% IRON TOXICITY. (Both heavy metals found in breast implants).It has only been two weeks since my explant surgery and from the moment I woke up I began to HEAL! Symptoms started going away IMMEDIATELY for me. The whites of my eyes were white again, my skin tone returned to normal, my face was producing oil again, my sinuses were clear, the painful throat and swollen tongue I had suffered with for more than 10 years were gone, my lymph nodes were no longer swollen and the inflammation in my face had disappeared. I have been able to eat so many foods I was intolerant to before with absolutely no adverse reaction. With every hour I feel better.
Dr Alex Grubnik
Dr Grubnick says that there can be complications with implants. They mostly rupture because the capsule that surrounds them puts pressure on the implant. The implant becomes painful and distorted. The capsule is the tissue that the body forms around the implant.
Two reasons to have implants, one is for size increase and the second after a mastectomy. 60% of women choose to have some reconstruction after mastectomy.We need to look at women who have had cancer and a compromised immune system and had implants and healthy women who have had implants.Breast Implants don’t last a life time and many women don’t know this. Aren’t properly briefed by doctor. Don’t know the dangers.
APRASSAGive us the history of breast implants/ banning of implants/guarentee now of health.

Script:


Breast Implant Illness

V/O
Women are very aware of the pressure society placed on them and they learn that they are often judged by their bodies. Through the lense of photoshopped perfection they place themselves under critical scrutiny and often feel that they can’t match up to the images they are exposed to daily.

Kalina
“I always felt out of proportion, I had the bottom half was always bigger than the top half and in this world if you don’t like something you can fix it.”

V/O
Kalina Chiminello had implants at the age of 19. Ashley Wagner was also wanted to have a fuller chest.

Ashley
“I was quite flat chested growing up , it was just a personal thing for me. And I was fortunate enough that for my 21st birthday my parents said you could have them done.”

Kalina
“Oh, I was in heaven I was so excited. I was finally going to have boobs.”

Link
It’s a multibillion dollar business breast augmentation is the most popular cosmetic surgical procedure, in 2019 about 1.8 million procedures were done, that’s around 5000 operations every day.”

https://www.statista.com/statistics/293437/leading-surgical-cosmetic-procedures/

V/O
Dr Chris Snijman is a plastic surgeon and the spokesperson for the regulatory body APRASSA, the Association of Plastic, Reconstructive and Aesthetic Surgeons of Southern Africa.

Claire
“What are some of the reasons why women would want to have a breast implant.”

Chris
“Essentially what are we looking for is an improvement in their torso, in their confidence in their self esteem.Obviously in the slightly older patient who has had lovely breasts prior to child bearing breast feeding and trying to restore themselves to their former glory.”

Claire
“Are breast implants forever?”

Chris
“No, nothing is forever..”

Claire
“Diamonds are..”

Chris
” No, no they require an upgrade…”

‘By far the majority of us will not be inserting a device that doesn’t have at least 10 years of data behind it.”

Alex
“Breast augmentation is the commonest procedure performed in the world and it’s also interestingly the procedure that results in the highest levels of patients satisfaction of all the plastic surgical procedures.”

V/O
Dr Alexandra Grubnik is a plastic and reconstructive surgeon at Milpark hospital. Before any surgery she ensures that her patients have all of the information they need and know exactly what to expect from breast surgery.


Alex “So there is a very good saying amongst surgeons, there is no surgery that is too minor so every single operation, no matter how small or short in duration, can always result in complications.

V/O
Kalina had her implants done in the Dubai, there were no complications and she healed very well.

Kalina
“I woke up from surgery and I looked down and I was ecstatic, I finally had boobs and I was going to go into life and I felt whole.”

V/O
How does the body react to the breast implant?

Chris
“The minute you insert this into the body the body is going to reject it. What the body does then is that it forms a very thin uniform membrane around the implant so that an encapsulates it. Every patients I going to develop that. That is your body ‘s natural response, why because it is protecting you from the implant and the implant from you.

V/O
The person who did Ashley’s operation was not a plastic surgeon but a doctor that she found on the East Rand.

Ashley
“Ja, I was super excited, I went in on the Monday for the consultation and I was booked that Friday for the operation.”

Claire
“Afterwards , in the few weeks afterwards were you happy?”

Ashley
“Yes, I was very happy , they looked great, the surgery went well, I healed well.”

V/O
But for both Ashley and Kalina the euphoria did not last long.

Claire
When did the problems start?

Kalina
“So I started getting rashes all over my face,”

Ashley
I started getting funny outbreaks from the chest up.

Kalina
I started getting food intolerances

Ashley
Every weeek, every month, there was an outbreak somehwere on my body, if not on my whole body, so it was psoriasis.

Kalina
My eyes it felt like they were going to bulge out of my head, there was so much pressure behind that gave me chronic migraines.

Link
Breast Implant Illness is a term that some women and doctors use to describe a wide range of debilitating symptoms that can occur after breast augmentation.

V/O
Breast Implant Illness seems to impact each individual in unique ways. Some of the symptoms include anxiety, hairloss, headaches, gastrointestinal issues, skin problems and dry eyes to name but a few.
V/O
There are tens of thousands of women around the world who have formed support groups on social forums all echoeing the same symtoms.
Claire
“What do you know and understand about Breast Implant Illness?

Chris
“You know this is not something that is new to us, so breast implant etc is basically not a recognised disease entitity in the true sense of the word, it is a name that has been given to a certain subset of patients with breast augmentation, silicone breast implants that will present with a certain constellation of symptoms.”

V/O
Both Kalina and Ashley spent tens of thousands of rands going from specialist to specialist to try and work out what was happening to their bodies.

Claire
“So when you got your psoriasis so did you immediately think your breast implants or …”

Ashley
“No not at all, firstly you don’t ever want to think its your implants, you are happy with getting something done, because it was skin I though hormones dermatologist..I went to about 4 different dermatologists.

Claire
“What did they say?”

Ashley
“They couldn’t give me an answer.”

Claire
“What was the medical advice that was given.”

Kalina
“What the diagnosticia said to me was that it is a developing auto immune disease, we’ll treat it when it’s there.”

V/O
Kalina describes living through hell for almost 10 years, it took a tremedous toll on her emotionally and physically.

Kalina
“I had given up, I had literally given up. I felt like some days I was dying.”

V/O
By chance she saw an Facebook post by playboy Hugh Hefner’s wife Crystal that said My Breast Implants Slowly Poisoned Me.

Kalina
“And that is when the penny dropped, I had every symptom she had mentioned. I cried because I did not want it to be so. Because I did not want to loose my boobs and I cried because I realised that there is a solution.”

Link
“The operation to remove an implant is called an explant and breast implant illness patients say that there health improved dramatically once their implants were removed.”

V/O
Ashley’s breast pain was increasing as the capsule around her breast had stated to shrink. It’s called capsular contraction – and by Dec last year Dr Grubnik performed an explant. Within days, the psoriasis cleared up.


Ashley
“There is no more infection in my body. In just 8 weeks since my op it’s like I am a different person.”

V/O
What she did find out was that the doctor had put implants into her that were manufactured in France, but banned in several countries including country of manufacture according to Ashley’s research.

Ashley
“This is not what I saw in the consultation room, what the doctor showed me he would be putting in me, once removing them I had definite leakage in my left breast, you can see that there,”



Alex
“So the implant is a medical device and as with any device there can be device failure, so it is very rare, the incidence is less than 2 % but the implants can rupture and they can leak.”

V/O
Medical grade silicone is commonly used in many implantable medical devices and is considered inert. Some implant manufacturers do offer a life time warranty.Dr Grubnik does stress that women should have imaging regularily to check their implants.

Alex
“However if you look at the FDA they say it is not a lifetime device so patients should be aware that they may need surther surgeries.”

V/O
So why do some women’s symptoms dissapear when their implants are removed.

Chris
“So because there might well be an association it doesn’t mean that there is cause and effect and over 400 peer reviewed clinical studies have been performed since the 1960’s , not one of them createing a link between silicone breats implanst and a distinct clinical entitiy. That doesn’t mean that it doesn’t exist.”

Link
“Having breast implants has changes millions of women’s lives in a positive way and although we struggle to get an on camera interview with an implant manufacturer, Mentor did send us this statement.”

V/O
The safety and clinical performance of Mentor breast implants is supported by completed and ongoing studies involving more than 200,000 women, including three, 10-year, prospective clinical trials.
Chris
“There is definitely a subset of patients that when you take these things out and when you take these things out they feel better. You can’t explain it. Might be a pristine implant and pristine pocket. We’ve all seen them in our practice.”
V/O
Neither Ashley nor Kalina had Mentor implants. Kalina’s implants had disintegrated so much that they could not find any serial number on it. Kalina had her explant 6 months ago and feels like a new woman now.
Kalina
“So I got wheeled into surgery and I wake up and I knew, that it was that. That this was my solution. I cannot explain the feeling to you. I looked down and I was at flat as a board. I’d say that 90% of my symptoms went away from that moment I woke up.”



Promo 1:
Some women with breast implants have been plagued by debilitating symptoms that medical professionals could not diagnose. They found answers ONLINE – a little-known condition called Breast Implant Illness.

Promo 2:
Studies have shown that breast implants can help boost self-esteem. But for some women they’ve come with a host of symptoms called Breast Implant Illness, that’s made their life a misery.

Promo 3:
A multi billion rand business, breast augmentation is the most popular cosmetic surgical procedure in the world. But some believe that their implants made them sick and they only got better when they were taken out.

Date: 0000-00-00 Script: Breast Implant Illness V/O Women are very aware of the pressure society placed on them and they learn that they are often judged by their bodies. Through the lense of photoshopped perfection they place themselves under critical scrutiny and often feel that they can’t match up to the images they are exposed to daily. Kalina “I always felt out of proportion, I had the bottom half was always bigger than the top half and in this world if you don’t like something you can fix it.” V/O Kalina Chiminello had implants at the age of 19. Ashley Wagner was also wanted to have a fuller chest. Ashley “I was quite flat chested growing up , it was just a personal thing for me. And I was fortunate enough that for my 21st birthday my parents said you could have them done.” Kalina “Oh, I was in heaven I was so excited. I was finally going to have boobs.” Link It’s a multibillion dollar business breast augmentation is the most popular cosmetic surgical procedure, in 2019 about 1.8 million procedures were done, that’s around 5000 operations every day.” https://www.statista.com/statistics/293437/leading-surgical-cosmetic-procedures/ V/O Dr Chris Snijman is a plastic surgeon and the spokesperson for the regulatory body APRASSA, the Association of Plastic, Reconstructive and Aesthetic Surgeons of Southern Africa. Claire “What are some of the reasons why women would want to have a breast implant.” Chris “Essentially what are we looking for is an improvement in their torso, in their confidence in their self esteem.Obviously in the slightly older patient who has had lovely breasts prior to child bearing breast feeding and trying to restore themselves to their former glory.” Claire “Are breast implants forever?” Chris “No, nothing is forever..” Claire “Diamonds are..” Chris ” No, no they require an upgrade…” ‘By far the majority of us will not be inserting a device that doesn’t have at least 10 years of data behind it.” Alex “Breast augmentation is the commonest procedure performed in the world and it’s also interestingly the procedure that results in the highest levels of patients satisfaction of all the plastic surgical procedures.” V/O Dr Alexandra Grubnik is a plastic and reconstructive surgeon at Milpark hospital. Before any surgery she ensures that her patients have all of the information they need and know exactly what to expect from breast surgery. Alex “So there is a very good saying amongst surgeons, there is no surgery that is too minor so every single operation, no matter how small or short in duration, can always result in complications. V/O Kalina had her implants done in the Dubai, there were no complications and she healed very well. Kalina “I woke up from surgery and I looked down and I was ecstatic, I finally had boobs and I was going to go into life and I felt whole.” V/O How does the body react to the breast implant? Chris “The minute you insert this into the body the body is going to reject it. What the body does then is that it forms a very thin uniform membrane around the implant so that an encapsulates it. Every patients I going to develop that. That is your body ‘s natural response, why because it is protecting you from the implant and the implant from you. V/O The person who did Ashley’s operation was not a plastic surgeon but a doctor that she found on the East Rand. Ashley “Ja, I was super excited, I went in on the Monday for the consultation and I was booked that Friday for the operation.” Claire “Afterwards , in the few weeks afterwards were you happy?” Ashley “Yes, I was very happy , they looked great, the surgery went well, I healed well.” V/O But for both Ashley and Kalina the euphoria did not last long. Claire When did the problems start? Kalina “So I started getting rashes all over my face,” Ashley I started getting funny outbreaks from the chest up. Kalina I started getting food intolerances Ashley Every weeek, every month, there was an outbreak somehwere on my body, if not on my whole body, so it was psoriasis. Kalina My eyes it felt like they were going to bulge out of my head, there was so much pressure behind that gave me chronic migraines. Link Breast Implant Illness is a term that some women and doctors use to describe a wide range of debilitating symptoms that can occur after breast augmentation. V/O Breast Implant Illness seems to impact each individual in unique ways. Some of the symptoms include anxiety, hairloss, headaches, gastrointestinal issues, skin problems and dry eyes to name but a few. V/O There are tens of thousands of women around the world who have formed support groups on social forums all echoeing the same symtoms. Claire “What do you know and understand about Breast Implant Illness? Chris “You know this is not something that is new to us, so breast implant etc is basically not a recognised disease entitity in the true sense of the word, it is a name that has been given to a certain subset of patients with breast augmentation, silicone breast implants that will present with a certain constellation of symptoms.” V/O Both Kalina and Ashley spent tens of thousands of rands going from specialist to specialist to try and work out what was happening to their bodies. Claire “So when you got your psoriasis so did you immediately think your breast implants or …” Ashley “No not at all, firstly you don’t ever want to think its your implants, you are happy with getting something done, because it was skin I though hormones dermatologist..I went to about 4 different dermatologists. Claire “What did they say?” Ashley “They couldn’t give me an answer.” Claire “What was the medical advice that was given.” Kalina “What the diagnosticia said to me was that it is a developing auto immune disease, we’ll treat it when it’s there.” V/O Kalina describes living through hell for almost 10 years, it took a tremedous toll on her emotionally and physically. Kalina “I had given up, I had literally given up. I felt like some days I was dying.” V/O By chance she saw an Facebook post by playboy Hugh Hefner’s wife Crystal that said My Breast Implants Slowly Poisoned Me. Kalina “And that is when the penny dropped, I had every symptom she had mentioned. I cried because I did not want it to be so. Because I did not want to loose my boobs and I cried because I realised that there is a solution.” Link “The operation to remove an implant is called an explant and breast implant illness patients say that there health improved dramatically once their implants were removed.” V/O Ashley’s breast pain was increasing as the capsule around her breast had stated to shrink. It’s called capsular contraction – and by Dec last year Dr Grubnik performed an explant. Within days, the psoriasis cleared up. Ashley “There is no more infection in my body. In just 8 weeks since my op it’s like I am a different person.” V/O What she did find out was that the doctor had put implants into her that were manufactured in France, but banned in several countries including country of manufacture according to Ashley’s research. Ashley “This is not what I saw in the consultation room, what the doctor showed me he would be putting in me, once removing them I had definite leakage in my left breast, you can see that there,” Alex “So the implant is a medical device and as with any device there can be device failure, so it is very rare, the incidence is less than 2 % but the implants can rupture and they can leak.” V/O Medical grade silicone is commonly used in many implantable medical devices and is considered inert. Some implant manufacturers do offer a life time warranty.Dr Grubnik does stress that women should have imaging regularily to check their implants. Alex “However if you look at the FDA they say it is not a lifetime device so patients should be aware that they may need surther surgeries.” V/O So why do some women’s symptoms dissapear when their implants are removed. Chris “So because there might well be an association it doesn’t mean that there is cause and effect and over 400 peer reviewed clinical studies have been performed since the 1960’s , not one of them createing a link between silicone breats implanst and a distinct clinical entitiy. That doesn’t mean that it doesn’t exist.” Link “Having breast implants has changes millions of women’s lives in a positive way and although we struggle to get an on camera interview with an implant manufacturer, Mentor did send us this statement.” V/O The safety and clinical performance of Mentor breast implants is supported by completed and ongoing studies involving more than 200,000 women, including three, 10-year, prospective clinical trials. Chris “There is definitely a subset of patients that when you take these things out and when you take these things out they feel better. You can’t explain it. Might be a pristine implant and pristine pocket. We’ve all seen them in our practice.” V/O Neither Ashley nor Kalina had Mentor implants. Kalina “So I got wheeled into surgery and I wake up and I knew, that it was that. That this was my solution. I cannot explain the feeling to you. I looked down and I was at flat as a board. I’d say that 90% of my symptoms went away from that moment I woke up.” Promo 1: Some women with breast implants have been plagued by debilitating symptoms that medical professionals could not diagnose. But for some women they’ve come with a host of symptoms called Breast Implant Illness, that’s made their life a misery. Promo 3: A multi billion rand business, breast augmentation is the most popular cosmetic surgical procedure in the world. But some believe that their implants made them sick and they only got better when they were taken out.

metadata.Summary: Breast implant illness (BII) is a term that some women and doctors use to refer to a wide range of symptoms that can develop after undergoing reconstruction or cosmetic augmentation with breast implants. It is also sometimes referred to as autoimmune/inflammatory syndrome induced by adjuvants (ASIA). BII can occur with any type of breast implant, including silicone gel-filled, saline-filled, smooth surface, textured surface, round, or teardrop-shaped.Two possible problems with breast implants: One is the condition Towt developed — breast implant illness (BII) — a cluster of symptoms such as fatigue, memory loss, and joint pain that can occur after getting breast implants and that frequently improve after the removal of the implants (explantation). Many of the symptoms of BII are the same as those of autoimmune and connective tissue disorders, such as lupus and rheumatoid arthritis. However, only some people who have BII get diagnosed with a specific autoimmune or connective tissue disorder. BII isn’t well understood and isn’t officially recognized as a medical condition, but some experts say it’s likely to be related to an autoimmune reaction to the implants. The other serious risk is a rare form of T-cell lymphoma (cancer of the immune system) called breast implant-associated anaplastic large cell lymphoma (BIA-ALCL) that develops in the scar tissue and fluid surrounding an implant. So far, all the confirmed cases of BIA-ALCL have been in women who had breast implants with a textured surface or whose implant surface type was not known. BIA-ALCL is curable in most patients if it’s diagnosed early and treated appropriately, but at least 33 women have died from the illness as of July 2019.2 Some patient activists call BIA-ALCL a “man-made cancer” because it’s linked to a specific medical device and was identified for the first time in 1997.
